stem_tex: The slope of the curve $y^3 - xy^2 = 4$ at the point where $y=2$ is
explanation_tex: At $y=2$, $8-4x=4$ gives $x=1$. Implicit differentiation gives $(3y^2-2xy)y\prime=y^2$, so $y\prime=4/(12-4)=1/2$.

stem_tex: The slope of the curve $y^2 - xy - 3x = 1$ at the point $(0,-1)$ is
explanation_tex: Implicit differentiation gives $(2y-x)y\prime=y+3$. At $(0,-1)$, the slope is $2/(-2)=-1$.

stem_tex: An equation of the tangent to $y=x\sin x$ at $(\pi/2,\pi/2)$ is
explanation_tex: The derivative is $y\prime=\sin x+x\cos x$, equal to $1$ at $x=\pi/2$. Thus $y-\pi/2=x-\pi/2$, or $y=x$.

stem_tex: The tangent to the curve of $y = xe^{-x}$ is horizontal when $x$ is equal to
explanation_tex: Differentiate to obtain $y\prime=e^{-x}(1-x)$. This vanishes only at $x=1$.

stem_tex: The minimum value of the slope of the curve $y = x^5 + x^3 - 2x$ is
explanation_tex: The slope is $5x^4+3x^2-2\ge-2$, with equality at $x=0$.

stem_tex: An equation of the tangent to the hyperbola $x^2-y^2=12$ at $(4,2)$ is
explanation_tex: Implicit differentiation gives $y\prime=x/y=2$. Thus $y-2=2(x-4)$, or $y=2x-6$.

stem_tex: A tangent to the curve $y^2-xy+9=0$ is vertical when
explanation_tex: The slope is $y\prime=y/(2y-x)$. A vertical tangent requires $x=2y$ with $y\ne0$. Substitution gives $9-y^2=0$, hence $y=\pm3$.

stem_tex: The volume of a sphere is given by $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$. Use a tangent line to approximate the increase in volume, in cubic inches, when the radius of a sphere is increased from 3 to 3.1 inches.
explanation_tex: Use $dV=4\pi r^2dr$ with $r=3$ and $dr=0.1$: $dV=4\pi(9)(0.1)=3.6\pi$ cubic inches.

stem_tex: When $x=3$, the equation $2x^2-y^3=10$ has the solution $y=2$. Using a tangent line to the graph of the curve, approximate $y$ when $x=3.04$.
explanation_tex: Implicit differentiation gives $y\prime=4x/(3y^2)=1$ at $(3,2)$. Thus $y\approx2+1(0.04)=2.04$.

stem_tex: If the side $e$ of a square is increased by 1%, then the area is increased approximately
explanation_tex: For $A=e^2$, $dA=2e\,de$. With $de=0.01e$, the approximate increase is $0.02e^2$.

stem_tex: The edge of a cube has length 10 in., with a possible error of 1%. The possible error, in cubic inches, in the volume of the cube is
explanation_tex: Using differentials, $dV=3e^2de=3(10)^2(0.01\cdot10)=30$ cubic inches. This is the approximate propagated error; the exact upper error is $10.1^3-10^3=30.301$.

stem_tex: The function $f(x) = x^4 - 4x^2$ has
choices_tex: one local minimum and two local maxima
one local minimum and no local maximum
no local minimum and one local maximum
two local minima and one local maximum
explanation_tex: The derivative $4x(x^2-2)$ changes signs $-,+,-,+$ at $-\sqrt2,0,\sqrt2$. Thus there are two local minima and one local maximum.

stem_tex: The number of inflection points on the graph of $f(x) = x^4 - 4x^2$ is
explanation_tex: The second derivative is $12x^2-8$, changing sign at $x=\pm\sqrt{2/3}$. There are two inflection points.

stem_tex: The maximum value of the function $y = -4\sqrt{2-x}$ is
explanation_tex: The real domain is $x\le2$. The function is nonpositive everywhere and equals $0$ at $x=2$, giving the maximum value $0$.

stem_tex: The total number of local maximum and minimum points of the function whose derivative, for all $x$, is given by $f'(x) = x(x-3)^2(x+1)^4$ is
explanation_tex: The even-power factors do not change sign at $-1$ or $3$. The derivative changes sign only at $x=0$, from negative to positive, so there is one local extremum.

stem_tex: For which curve shown below are both $f'$ and $f''$ negative?
explanation_tex: Curve D decreases as $x$ increases, so $f\prime<0$. Its slopes become increasingly negative, showing concavity down and $f\prime\prime<0$.

figure.alt: Four source curves labeled A,B,C,D: decreasing concave up, increasing concave up, increasing concave down, decreasing concave down.

stem_tex: For which curve shown below is $f\prime\prime$ positive but $f\prime$ negative?
explanation_tex: Curve A is decreasing, so $f\prime<0$, but its slopes become less negative as $x$ increases, so $f\prime\prime>0$.

figure.alt: Four source curves labeled A,B,C,D: decreasing concave up, increasing concave up, increasing concave down, decreasing concave down.

stem_tex: The position of a particle moving along a horizontal line is $s=t^3-6t^2+12t-8$. The object is moving to the right for
explanation_tex: Velocity is $s\prime=3t^2-12t+12=3(t-2)^2$, positive for every $t\ne2$.

stem_tex: The position of a particle moving along a horizontal line is $s=t^3-6t^2+12t-8$. The minimum value of the speed is
explanation_tex: Speed is $3(t-2)^2\ge0$, and its minimum $0$ occurs at $t=2$.

stem_tex: The position of a particle moving along a horizontal line is $s=t^3-6t^2+12t-8$. The acceleration is positive
explanation_tex: Acceleration is $s\prime\prime=6(t-2)$, positive exactly for $t>2$.

stem_tex: The position of a particle moving along a horizontal line is $s=t^3-6t^2+12t-8$. The speed of the particle is decreasing for
explanation_tex: Velocity is positive away from $t=2$, so speed decreases when acceleration $6(t-2)$ is negative, namely $t<2$.

stem_tex: A particle moves along a horizontal line with position $s=t^4-6t^3+12t^2+3$ at time $t$. The particle is at rest when $t$ is equal to
explanation_tex: Velocity is $2t(2t^2-9t+12)$. The quadratic discriminant is $81-96<0$ and it is positive everywhere, so only $t=0$ gives rest.

stem_tex: A particle moves along a horizontal line with position $s=t^4-6t^3+12t^2+3$ at time $t$. The velocity, $v$, is increasing when
explanation_tex: Acceleration is $12t^2-36t+24=12(t-1)(t-2)$. It is positive on $t<1$ or $t>2$, where velocity increases.

stem_tex: A particle moves along a horizontal line with position $s=t^4-6t^3+12t^2+3$ at time $t$. The speed of the particle is increasing for
explanation_tex: Velocity $2t(2t^2-9t+12)$ has the sign of $t$. Acceleration $12(t-1)(t-2)$ shares its sign precisely on $(0,1)$ and $(2,\infty)$, so speed increases there.

stem_tex: The displacement from the origin of a particle moving on a line is given by $s = t^4-4t^3$. The maximum displacement during the time interval $-2 \leq t \leq 4$ is
explanation_tex: Critical times satisfy $s\prime=4t^2(t-3)=0$. Evaluate $s$ at $-2,0,3,4$: the values are $48,0,-27,0$. The maximum is $48$.

stem_tex: If a particle moves along a line according to the law $s = t^5+5t^4$, then the number of times it reverses direction is
explanation_tex: Velocity is $5t^3(t+4)$ and changes sign at both $t=-4$ and $t=0$. Hence there are two reversals over all real times. No restriction to nonnegative times is stated.

stem_tex: The position vector of a moving point is $\mathbf R(t)=\langle3\cos(\pi t/3),2\sin(\pi t/3)\rangle$. A single equation in $x$ and $y$ for its path is
explanation_tex: Eliminate the parameter with $x^2/9+y^2/4=\cos^2(\pi t/3)+\sin^2(\pi t/3)=1$, giving $4x^2+9y^2=36$.

stem_tex: The position vector of a moving point is $\mathbf R(t)=\langle3\cos(\pi t/3),2\sin(\pi t/3)\rangle$. When $t=3$, the speed of the particle is
explanation_tex: Velocity is $\langle-\pi\sin(\pi t/3),(2\pi/3)\cos(\pi t/3)\rangle$. At $t=3$, it is $\langle0,-2\pi/3\rangle$, with magnitude $2\pi/3$.

stem_tex: The position vector of a moving point is $\mathbf R(t)=\langle3\cos(\pi t/3),2\sin(\pi t/3)\rangle$. The magnitude of the acceleration when $t=3$ is
explanation_tex: Acceleration is $\langle-(\pi^2/3)\cos(\pi t/3),-(2\pi^2/9)\sin(\pi t/3)\rangle$. At $t=3$ its magnitude is $\pi^2/3$.

stem_tex: The position vector of a moving point is $\mathbf R(t)=\langle3\cos(\pi t/3),2\sin(\pi t/3)\rangle$. At $t=1/2$, the slope of the curve is
explanation_tex: The slope is $(dy/dt)/(dx/dt)=-(2/3)\cot(\pi t/3)$. At $t=1/2$, the angle is $\pi/6$, giving slope $-2\sqrt3/3$.

stem_tex: A balloon is being filled with helium at the rate of 4 ft$^3$/min. The rate, in square feet per minute, at which the surface area is increasing when the volume is $\dfrac{32\pi}{3}$ ft$^3$ is
explanation_tex: For a sphere, $4\pi r^3/3=32\pi/3$ gives $r=2$. Since $dA/dV=2/r=1$, the area increases at $1\cdot4=4$ square feet per minute.

stem_tex: A circular conical reservoir, vertex down, has depth 20 ft and radius at the top 10 ft. Water is leaking out so that the surface is falling at the rate of $\dfrac{1}{2}$ ft/hr. The rate, in cubic feet per hour, at which the water is leaving the reservoir when the water is 8 ft deep is
explanation_tex: Similar triangles give $r=h/2$, so $V=\pi h^3/12$. Therefore $V\prime=(\pi h^2/4)h\prime=(\pi\cdot64/4)(-1/2)=-8\pi$; water leaves at $8\pi$ cubic feet per hour.

stem_tex: A local minimum value of the function $y = \dfrac{e^x}{x}$ is
explanation_tex: The derivative $e^x(x-1)/x^2$ changes from negative to positive at $x=1$. The local minimum value is $e$.

stem_tex: The area of the largest rectangle that can be drawn with one side along the $x$-axis and two vertices on the curve of $y = e^{-x^2}$ is
explanation_tex: For half-width $x>0$, area is $A=2xe^{-x^2}$ and $A\prime=2e^{-x^2}(1-2x^2)$. The unique maximum occurs at $x=1/\sqrt2$, with area $\sqrt{2/e}$.

stem_tex: A line with a negative slope is drawn through the point $(1,2)$ forming a right triangle with the positive $x$- and $y$-axes. The slope of the line forming the triangle of least area is
explanation_tex: Write the slope as $-k$, $k>0$. The intercepts are $1+2/k$ and $2+k$, so area is $2+k/2+2/k$. Its derivative $1/2-2/k^2$ changes from negative to positive at $k=2$, giving slope $-2$.

stem_tex: The point(s) on the curve $x^2-y^2=4$ closest to the point $(6,0)$ is (are)
explanation_tex: Squared distance is $(x-6)^2+y^2=(x-6)^2+x^2-4=2(x-3)^2+14$. Its minimum occurs at $x=3$, where $y=\pm\sqrt5$.

stem_tex: The sum of the squares of two positive numbers is 200; their minimum product is
explanation_tex: Both numbers must be positive, so their product is positive. Taking one arbitrarily close to $0$ makes the product approach $0$, but never attain it. The infimum is $0$ and there is no minimum.

stem_tex: The first-quadrant point on the curve $y^2x = 18$ that is closest to the point $(2,0)$ is
explanation_tex: Use $y^2=18/x$ to minimize $D^2=(x-2)^2+18/x$ on $x>0$. Its derivative is $2(x-2)-18/x^2$, zero at $x=3$. Since $(D^2)\prime\prime=2+36/x^3>0$, the minimum is $(3,\sqrt6)$.

stem_tex: If $h$ is a small negative number, then the local linear approximation for $\sqrt[3]{27+h}$ is
If $f(x) = xe^{-x}$, then at $x=0$
explanation_tex: The derivative is $e^{-x}(1-x)$, equal to $1>0$ at $x=0$. Hence $f$ is increasing near $0$.

stem_tex: A function $f$ has a derivative for each $x$ such that $|x|<2$ and has a local minimum at $(2,-5)$. Which statement below must be true?
choices_tex: none of the preceding is necessarily true
explanation_tex: Differentiability is assumed only for $|x|<2$, not at $x=2$. The example $f(x)=|x-2|-5$ has the given minimum but no derivative at $2$. A local minimum also does not force the global signs stated in C.

stem_tex: The height of a rectangular box is 10 in. Its length increases at 2 in./sec and its width decreases at 4 in./sec. When the length is 8 in. and width is 6 in., the volume changes at how many cubic inches per second?
explanation_tex: With $V=10lw$, product differentiation gives $V\prime=10(l\prime w+lw\prime)=10(2\cdot6+8(-4))=-200$.

stem_tex: The tangent to $x^3+x^2y+4y=1$ at $(3,-2)$ has slope
explanation_tex: Implicit differentiation gives $3x^2+2xy+(x^2+4)y\prime=0$. At $(3,-2)$, the slope is $-(27-12)/(9+4)=-15/13$.

stem_tex: If $f(x) = ax^4+bx^2$ and $ab>0$, then
choices_tex: the curve has no horizontal tangents
the curve is concave up for all $x$
the curve has no inflection point
none of the preceding is necessarily true
explanation_tex: The second derivative is $12ax^2+2b$. Since $ab>0$, both terms have the same nonzero sign, so concavity never changes and there is no inflection point.

stem_tex: A function $f$ is continuous and differentiable on the interval $[0,4]$, where $f'$ is positive but $f''$ is negative. Which table could represent points on $f$?
explanation_tex: For equal $x$ steps, increasing and strictly concave-down values have positive, decreasing secant slopes. Only C has successive increases $8,6,4,2$.

stem_tex: An equation of the tangent to the curve with parametric equations $x = 2t+1$, $y = 3-t^3$ at the point where $t=1$ is
Given $f(x)=\sqrt[3]x$ and $f(64)=4$, use the tangent line to estimate how much less than $4$ is $\sqrt[3]{63}$.
explanation_tex: The tangent slope at $64$ is $1/(3\cdot64^{2/3})=1/48$. A decrease of $1$ in $x$ produces an approximate decrease of $1/48$ in the cube root.

stem_tex: The best linear approximation for $f(x) = \tan x$ near $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ is $y=$
explanation_tex: At $a=\pi/4$, $\tan a=1$ and $\sec^2a=2$. Therefore $L(x)=1+2(x-\pi/4)$.

stem_tex: Given $f(x) = e^{kx}$, approximate $f(h)$, where $h$ is near zero, using a tangent-line approximation. $f(h) \approx$
explanation_tex: Since $f(0)=1$ and $f'(0)=k$, the tangent approximation is $f(h)\approx1+kh$.

stem_tex: If $f(x) = cx^2+dx+e$ for the function shown in the graph, then
explanation_tex: The graph is concave down, so $f''=2c<0$. Its slope at $0$ is negative, so $d=f'(0)<0$, and the positive vertical intercept gives $e=f(0)>0$.

stem_tex: Given $f(x) = \log_{10}x$ and $\log_{10}(102) \approx 2.0086$, which is closest to $f'(100)$?
explanation_tex: The nearby secant estimate is $f\prime(100)\approx(2.0086-2)/(102-100)=0.0043$.

stem_tex: The point on $y=\sqrt{2x+1}$ where the tangent is parallel to $x-3y=6$ is
explanation_tex: The line has slope $1/3$. Set $y\prime=1/\sqrt{2x+1}=1/3$, giving $x=4$, $y=3$.

stem_tex: An equation of the tangent to $x^2=4y$ at the point where $x=-2$ is
explanation_tex: At $x=-2$, $y=1$ and $y\prime=x/2=-1$. The tangent is $y-1=-(x+2)$, or $x+y+1=0$.

stem_tex: The table shows velocity at time $t$ for an object moving along a line. Estimate acceleration in ft/sec$^2$ at $t=6$ sec. $\begin{array}{c|rrrr}t\ (\mathrm{sec})&0&4&8&10\\v&18&16&10&0\end{array}$
explanation_tex: The centered secant estimate is $(v(8)-v(4))/(8-4)=(10-16)/4=-1.5$ ft/sec$^2$.

stem_tex: The figure shows $f\prime$ on $[0,7]$. From the graph it follows that
explanation_tex: The graph is of $f\prime$, positive between $2$ and $3$. Hence $f$ increases there and $f(2)<f(3)$.

stem_tex: The figure shows $f\prime$ on $[0,7]$. Which statement best describes $f$ at $x=5$?
choices_tex: The graph of $f$ has a point of inflection.
explanation_tex: At $x=5$, $f\prime$ changes from positive to negative. By the first-derivative test, $f$ has a maximum there.

stem_tex: The figure shows $f\prime$ on $[0,7]$. For which interval is the graph of $f$ concave downward?
explanation_tex: The derivative decreases on the whole interval $(4,7)$, so $f$ is concave down there. D is the maximal listed interval; B and C are also subintervals of concavity.
source_correction: D is the maximal interval; B and C are also contained in the concave-down interval.

stem_tex: The figure shows velocity in ft/sec on $0\le t\le5$. The object attains its maximum speed when $t=$
explanation_tex: The largest magnitude of velocity is $10$ ft/sec, attained when $v=-10$ at $t=3$. Since speed is $|v|$, this is the maximum speed.

stem_tex: The figure shows velocity in ft/sec on $0\le t\le5$. The speed of the object is increasing during the time interval
explanation_tex: On $(2,3)$ the velocity is negative and becomes more negative. Hence its magnitude, the speed, increases.

stem_tex: The figure shows velocity in ft/sec on $0\le t\le5$. The acceleration of the object is positive during the time interval
explanation_tex: Acceleration is the slope of the velocity graph. The only segment with positive slope is $(3,5)$.

stem_tex: The figure shows velocity in ft/sec on $0\le t\le5$. How many times on $0<t<5$ is the object's acceleration undefined?
explanation_tex: The velocity graph has corners at $t=1,2,3$, where the one-sided slopes differ. Acceleration is undefined at these three times.

stem_tex: The figure shows velocity in ft/sec on $0\le t\le5$. During $2<t<3$, the object's acceleration (in ft/sec$^2$) is
explanation_tex: On $(2,3)$ the velocity graph has slope $(v(3)-v(2))/(3-2)=(-10-0)/1=-10$ ft/sec$^2$.

stem_tex: The figure shows velocity in ft/sec on $0\le t\le5$. The object is farthest to the right when $t=$
explanation_tex: Velocity is positive before $t=2$ and negative after it. Position therefore increases to $t=2$ and then decreases, so the object is farthest right at $t=2$.

stem_tex: The figure shows velocity in ft/sec on $0\le t\le5$. The object's average acceleration (in ft/sec$^2$) for the interval $0 \leq t \leq 3$ is
explanation_tex: Average acceleration is $(v(3)-v(0))/3=(-10-5)/3=-5$ ft/sec$^2$.

stem_tex: The line $y=3x+k$ is tangent to the curve $y=x^3$ when $k$ is equal to
explanation_tex: Tangency requires $3x^2=3$, so $x=\pm1$. The intercept $k=x^3-3x$ is $-2$ or $2$.

stem_tex: The two tangents that can be drawn from the point $(3,5)$ to the parabola $y=x^2$ have slopes
explanation_tex: The tangent at $x=a$ is $y=2ax-a^2$. Passing through $(3,5)$ gives $a^2-6a+5=0$, hence $a=1,5$ and slopes $2,10$.

stem_tex: The table shows velocity for an object moving along a line. Estimate acceleration in ft/sec$^2$ at $t=1$. $\begin{array}{c|rrrr}t\ (\mathrm{sec})&1.0&1.5&2.2&2.5\\v\ (\mathrm{ft/sec})&12.2&13.0&13.4&13.7\end{array}$
explanation_tex: Use the closest forward secant: $(13.0-12.2)/(1.5-1.0)=1.6$ ft/sec$^2$.

stem_tex: For $0<x<4$, $f\prime(x)=x\sin x-\cos x$. $f$ has a local maximum when $x$ is approximately
explanation_tex: Solving $x\sin x-\cos x=0$ numerically gives a root near $3.425618$ where $f\prime$ changes from positive to negative. Thus the local maximum occurs near $x=3.426$.

stem_tex: For $0<x<4$, $f\prime(x)=x\sin x-\cos x$. The graph of $f$ has a point of inflection when $x$ is approximately
explanation_tex: The second derivative is $2\sin x+x\cos x$. It changes sign at its zero $x\approx2.288930$, giving an inflection point near $2.289$.

stem_tex: A particle has position $x=2t$, $y=4t-t^2$. The particle moves along
explanation_tex: Eliminate $t=x/2$ to obtain $y=2x-x^2/4$, a parabola.

stem_tex: A particle has position $x=2t$, $y=4t-t^2$. The speed of the particle at any time $t$ is
explanation_tex: Velocity is $\langle2,4-2t\rangle$, whose magnitude is $\sqrt{4+(4-2t)^2}=2\sqrt{t^2-4t+5}$.

stem_tex: A particle has position $x=2t$, $y=4t-t^2$. The minimum speed of the particle is
explanation_tex: Speed is $\sqrt{4+(4-2t)^2}\ge2$, with equality at $t=2$. The minimum speed is $2$.

stem_tex: A particle has position $x=2t$, $y=4t-t^2$. The acceleration of the particle
choices_tex: is constant both in magnitude and in direction
explanation_tex: Differentiating position twice gives acceleration $\langle0,-2\rangle$, constant in both magnitude and direction.

stem_tex: If a particle moves along a curve with constant speed, then
choices_tex: the magnitude of its acceleration must equal zero
the direction of acceleration must be constant
the curve along which the particle moves must be a straight line
its velocity and acceleration vectors must be perpendicular
explanation_tex: Constant speed implies $\mathbf v\cdot\mathbf v$ is constant. Differentiating gives $2\mathbf v\cdot\mathbf a=0$, so the velocity and acceleration vectors are orthogonal.

stem_tex: A particle moves on $y=2x-\ln x$ with $dx/dt=-2$ at all times. At $(1,2)$, $dy/dt$ is
explanation_tex: The chain rule gives $dy/dt=(2-1/x)\,dx/dt$. At $x=1$ this is $(2-1)(-2)=-2$.

stem_tex: A particle moves on $r=6\cos2\theta$, with $d\theta/dt=1/3$ radian/sec when $\theta=\pi/6$. At $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$, find the rate of change (in units per second) of the particle's distance from the origin.
explanation_tex: Here $r=6\cos(\pi/3)=3>0$, so distance is $r$. Differentiate: $dr/dt=(-12\sin2\theta)(1/3)=-4\sin(\pi/3)=-2\sqrt3$.

stem_tex: A particle moves on $r=6\cos2\theta$, with $d\theta/dt=1/3$ radian/sec when $\theta=\pi/6$. At $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$, what is the horizontal component of the particle's velocity?
explanation_tex: Since $x=r\cos\theta$, $x\prime=r\prime\cos\theta-r\sin\theta\,\theta\prime$. At $\pi/6$, $r=3$, $r\prime=-2\sqrt3$, and $\theta\prime=1/3$, giving $x\prime=-3-1/2=-7/2$.

stem_tex: The figure shows $f\prime$ on $[0,5]$. $f$ has a local minimum at $x=$
explanation_tex: At $x=1$, $f'$ changes from negative to positive, giving a local minimum of $f$. At $x=3$ it touches zero without changing sign.

stem_tex: The figure shows $f\prime$ on $[0,5]$. The graph of $f$ has a point of inflection at $x=$
explanation_tex: Inflection points of $f$ occur where $f\prime$ changes from increasing to decreasing or vice versa. The graph of $f\prime$ has a local maximum at $x=2$ and minimum at $x=3$, so both are inflection locations for $f$.

figure.alt: Derivative crosses zero at 1, has local maximum at 2 and local minimum zero at 3.

choices_tex: $f$ is continuous but not differentiable at $x=a$
The graph of $f$ has a point of inflection at $x=a$

stem_tex: A vertical circular cylinder has radius $r$ ft and height $h$ ft. If the height and radius both increase at the constant rate of 2 ft/sec, then the rate, in square feet per second, at which the lateral surface area increases is
explanation_tex: Lateral area is $A=2\pi rh$. Differentiating gives $A\prime=2\pi(r\prime h+rh\prime)=4\pi(r+h)$.

stem_tex: A tangent drawn to the parabola $y=4-x^2$ at the point $(1,3)$ forms a right triangle with the coordinate axes. The area of the triangle is
explanation_tex: The slope is $-2x=-2$ at $x=1$. The tangent is $y=-2x+5$, with intercepts $5$ and $5/2$. Thus its triangle has area $\frac12(5)(5/2)=25/4$.

stem_tex: Two cars are traveling along perpendicular roads, car $A$ at 40 mph and car $B$ at 60 mph. At noon, when car $A$ reaches the intersection, car $B$ is 90 miles away, and moving toward the intersection. At 1 P.M. the rate, in miles per hour, at which the distance between the cars is changing is
explanation_tex: At 1 P.M., $x=40$, $y=30$, and separation $d=50$. From $d^2=x^2+y^2$, $d\prime=(xx\prime+yy\prime)/d=(40\cdot40+30(-60))/50=-4$ mph.

stem_tex: Two cars are traveling along perpendicular roads, car $A$ at 40 mph and car $B$ at 60 mph. At noon, when car $A$ reaches the intersection, car $B$ is 90 miles away and moving toward the intersection. If $t$ represents the time, in hours, traveled after noon, then the cars are closest together when $t$ is
explanation_tex: Minimize squared separation $(40t)^2+(90-60t)^2$. Setting the derivative to zero gives $10400t-10800=0$, so $t=27/26\approx1.038$ hours.

stem_tex: The figure shows velocity in ft/sec on $0\le t\le12$. For what $t$ does this object attain its maximum acceleration?
explanation_tex: Acceleration is the slope of velocity. The graph has zero slope on $(0,4)$, positive constant slope on $(4,8)$, and negative slope after $8$. Its maximum occurs throughout $(4,8)$.

figure.alt: Velocity is constant negative to t=4, crosses zero at 5, peaks at 8, then decreases staying positive.

stem_tex: Given $f\prime$ as graphed, which could be the graph of $f$?
explanation_tex: The derivative is positive before $1$, negative between $1$ and $3$, and zero at $1$ and $3$. Thus $f$ increases to a smooth maximum at $1$, then decreases and flattens at $3$. Also $f\prime$ decreases until $2$ and increases afterward, so $f$ changes from concave down to concave up at $2$. Only graph C has all these features.

stem_tex: If $f(6)=30$ and $f\prime(x)=x^2/(x+3)$, estimate $f(6.02)$ using the tangent line at $x=6$.
explanation_tex: The tangent slope is $f\prime(6)=36/9=4$. Thus $f(6.02)\approx30+4(0.02)=30.08$.
